title: Absolute zero is a limit you may approach, never reach
body: The third law of thermodynamics (Nernst) implies cooling to exactly zero kelvin would need infinitely many steps; each refrigeration cycle removes a fraction of what remains. Laboratories reach billionths of a kelvin asymptotically. The coldest known natural place, the Boomerang Nebula, sits around one kelvin, warmed by the cosmic background above absolute zero regardless.
